testcases.Feature: Independent control register for each GPIO
testcases.Test Description: Verifies reset values and read/write behavior of per-pin and group GPIO registers by reading masked defaults, then writing multiple patterns with mask-aware expectations and comparing readbacks to expected results. Skips registers called out in the test data.
testcases.Remarks: Default-value comparison explicitly ignores the least significant bit of reads. Certain registers are excluded from default and/or R/W checks as specified by skip arrays.
testcases.Test Steps / Procedure:
Entry and control flow
1) Enter the test through the single test entry.
2) Run the default/reset value verification before any write/read tests.
3) After completing default checks, execute the write/read verification against multiple data patterns.
4) Decide final pass/fail based on accumulated comparison results.

Default/reset value verification
5) For each register in the configured list, if it is marked to be skipped for default checks, continue to the next.
6) If the register is not readable per its mask, continue to the next.
7) Read the register value and ignore the least significant bit of the read result.
8) Compare this masked value with the recorded default for that register and record a failure on any mismatch.

Write and read verification
9) For each predefined data pattern, set the current write value to that pattern.
10) For each register in the list, if it is marked to be skipped, continue to the next.
11) If the register is not writable per its mask, continue to the next.
12) Write the current pattern masked by the register’s write mask to that register.
13) After completing writes for the current pattern, iterate the same register list for readback.
14) For each register, if skipped or not writable or not readable per its respective masks, continue to the next.
15) Read the register and apply the read mask to the read value.
16) Form the expected value by combining the written bits (limited by both read and write masks) with the preserved default for write-protected bits.
17) Compare the masked read value with the expected value and record a failure upon mismatch.

Completion
18) If any failure was recorded in either the default or the write/read checks, the test result is fail; otherwise pass.

testcases.Feature: Independent GPIO control Register field neie (Type: R/W, Reset: 0x0).
testcases.Test Description: Enables falling-edge interrupts on inputs for a sweep of 32 pins, synthesizes one falling transition per pin using a pad-control address, then validates pin input state and masked group status, and clears interrupt states through the GPIO group, system interrupt register, and the interrupt controller.
testcases.Remarks: The interrupt line selection depends on a build-time option to target one of two banks. The test uses bounded waits with a timeout to avoid hanging while waiting for the handler.
testcases.Test Steps / Procedure:
Entry and setup
1) Enter the test through the single test entry.
2) Enable the interrupt line associated with the selected GPIO bank in the interrupt controller.
3) Enable the corresponding system-level interrupt output.
4) Initialize pad control to a high level so that a later low drive produces a falling transition.

Per-pin configuration
5) For each pin in the 32-pin sweep, configure input mode and enable falling-edge interrupt; also clear any per-pin raw status, inserting a small delay after each configuration write.

Per-pin test loop
6) For each pin index in the sweep: clear the group raw status bit for that pin, enable only that pin in the group interrupt enable register, and delay briefly.
7) Arm the pending flag before transition generation to avoid a race.
8) Generate a falling edge for the active pin by first setting all pads high, waiting briefly, and then driving only the active pin low.
9) Poll for the handler to clear the pending flag with a fixed delay per iteration and a finite iteration budget; on timeout, record an error for the current pin and continue.

Interrupt handling and clear
10) In the handler for the active pin: confirm the pin input reads low after the falling edge, confirm the masked group status for the active pin is asserted, then clear both the per-pin raw status and the group raw status bit.
11) Verify that the masked group status returns to zero after the clear.
12) Clear the corresponding system raw status bit and the interrupt controller entry.

Completion
13) After all pins have been exercised, return a passing result if no errors were recorded; otherwise, return failure.

testcases.Feature: Independent GPIO control Register field peie (Type: R/W, Reset: 0x0).
testcases.Test Description: Enables rising-edge interrupts on inputs for a sweep of 32 pins, configures input mode through group control, synthesizes one rising transition per pin using a pad-control address, verifies masked group status, then clears per-pin raw status and system raw status before re-enabling the group.
testcases.Remarks: The interrupt line selection depends on a build-time option to target one of two banks. The test masks the group interrupt during service and uses a bounded wait with timeout for each pin.
testcases.Test Steps / Procedure:
Entry and setup
1) Enter the test through the single test entry.
2) Enable the interrupt line associated with the selected GPIO bank in the interrupt controller.
3) Enable the corresponding system-level interrupt output.

Per-pin and group configuration
4) For each pin in the 32-pin sweep, enable rising-edge interrupt in the per-pin control register.
5) Configure group input mode for the four groups covering the 32 pins.
6) Enable the group interrupt for all pins in the first group enable register.

Per-pin test loop
7) For each pin index in the sweep: force the pad control low, wait briefly, arm the pending flag, then set the pad control high to create a rising transition.
8) Poll for the handler to clear the pending flag with a fixed delay per iteration and a finite iteration budget; on timeout, record an error and exit the loop.
9) Drive the pad control low again and pause briefly to prepare for the next iteration.

Interrupt handling and clear
10) In the handler, read the masked group status and temporarily mask the group output to prevent re-entry while servicing.
11) If the masked group status is non-zero, proceed; otherwise record an error.
12) Clear per-pin raw status across the bank, delay briefly, then verify that the masked group status returns to zero.
13) Clear the corresponding system raw status bit and verify it is cleared on readback.
14) Re-enable the group interrupt and clear the interrupt controller entry.

Completion
15) After all pins have been processed (or upon the first timeout), return pass if no errors were recorded; otherwise fail.

testcases.Hidden_Test_Description: Per-pin posedge interrupt test on GPIOs 8..39. Enables peie by writing 0x00020000 to each per-pin control register, sets group IO control to 0xFF for inputs, enables group interrupts, then drives 0xA0243ffc low->high per iteration. ISR masks group, verifies GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 non-zero, clears per-pin iclr (0x00010000) for all pins, checks group status == 0, clears sysreg RAW_STCR1 bit, re-enables group, and clears GIC.
testcases.Hidden_Remarks: GPIO0 or GPIO1 macro selects GIC IRQ and system interrupt bits. Timeout is 2000 iterations with wait_on(10) per loop. ISR masks group enable during service and re-enables after clear.
testcases.Hidden_Test_Steps_Procedure:
Entry: void test_case()
1. If GPIO0: GIC_EnableIRQ(87); if GPIO1: GIC_EnableIRQ(88).
2. test_err = 0.
3. If GPIO0: write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO0_INTR); if GPIO1: write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1, LSS_SYSREG_INTR_EN1_GPIO1_INTR).
4. for (i=0; i<32; i++): write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (i*4), 0x00020000); // enable peie
5. wait_on(10).
6. write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1, 0x000000FF); write_reg(GROUP2, 0x000000FF); write_reg(GROUP3, 0x000000FF); write_reg(GROUP4, 0x000000FF).
7. wait_on(10).
8. write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, 0xFFFFFFFF).
9. for (i=0; i<32; i++):
10.  write_reg(0xA0243ffc, 0x00000000); wait_on(10); int_pend = 1; write_reg(0xA0243ffc, 0xFFFFFFFF);
11.  int timeout = 2000; while ((int_pend == 1) && (--timeout > 0)) { wait_on(10); }
12.  if (timeout == 0) { printf timeout; test_err++; break; }
13.  write_reg(0xA0243ffc, 0x00000000); wait_on(10);
14. finish(test_err).

ISR: void Default_IRQHandler()
15. wr_val = 1 << i; int_pend = 0.
16. rdata_grp = read_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1).
17. write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, 0x00000000).
18. if ((rdata_grp & 0xffffffff) != 0) { /* ok */ } else { printf error; test_err++; }
19. for (j=0; j<32; j++): write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_GPIO_8 + (j*4), 0x00010000); // iclr per pin
20. wait_on(2).
21. rdata_grp = read_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1); if (rdata_grp == 0x0) { /* ok */ } else { printf error; test_err++; }
22. If GPIO0: write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR); rdata=read_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1); if ((rdata & LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO0_INTR) != 0) test_err++.
23. If GPIO1: write_reg(MIZAR_LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1, LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR); rdata=read_reg(...); if ((rdata & LSS_SYSREG_RAW_STCR1_GPIO1_INTR) != 0) test_err++.
24. write_reg(MIZAR_GPIO_GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1, 0xFFFFFFFF).
25. If GPIO0: GIC_ClearIRQ(87); If GPIO1: GIC_ClearIRQ(88).
